t: Apply Operations to Make Sum of Array Greater Than or Equal to k
o: Starting from [1], each operation either increments one element by 1 or duplicates one element. We want the minimum number of operations to reach a total sum ≥ k. Intuitively we should first grow one element to some value v (cost v−1 increments), then duplicate it until we have enough copies (cost ⌈k/v⌉−1 duplications), since mixing increments after duplication wastes work. Example 1: v = 4 costs 3 increments, then 2 duplications give 4+4+4 = 12 ≥ 11 — total 5. Example 2: k = 1 already holds, answer 0. Since all copies should be equal in an optimal plan, enumerating the final value v finds the optimum.
k: In an optimal plan, increment first, then duplicate: all final elements equal some value v ≥ 1.
Total cost for target value v is (v − 1) + (⌈k/v⌉ − 1); minimizing over v gives the answer, and the optimum lies near √k.

a.n: Approach 1: Enumerate the final element value
a.i: Fix the final common value v. Reaching one copy of v costs v−1 increments; producing ⌈k/v⌉ copies costs ⌈k/v⌉−1 duplications. Any interleaving cannot beat doing all increments first (increments applied before duplication multiply their effect). Trying every v from 1 to k covers all plausible plans.
s: Initialize best = k − 1 (the v = 1 plan: duplicate k−1 times).
For each v in 1..k, compute cost = (v − 1) + (⌈k/v⌉ − 1) and update best.
a.t: O(k) — one pass over candidate values up to 10⁵.

a.i: The cost v + ⌈k/v⌉ − 2 is a discretized v + k/v, minimized near v = √k. So it suffices to try v in [1, ⌊√(2k)⌋ + 2] (or a small window around √k), reducing the enumeration to O(√k) while remaining provably correct since the function decreases then increases.
a.t: O(√k) — the unimodal cost means only values up to ~√(2k) need testing.

w: Present the 'increment then duplicate' exchange argument first — it is the crux: an increment done after a duplication could have been done before, affecting more copies. Then either full enumeration (simplest, safely fast here) or the √k-window refinement. Pitfall: off-by-one on the ceiling ⌈k/v⌉ (use integer (k+v−1)//v) and remembering v = 1 (pure duplication) and the k = 1 case (zero operations). Follow-up: what if duplication doubles the whole array instead of copying one element — then think in terms of doubling/incrementing a single counter (binary representation of k).
